name: Carboprost
mechanism: Synthetic 15-methyl analogue of prostaglandin F2α. Stimulates myometrial contraction via PGF2α receptors, increasing uterine tone and contractions. Promotes haemostasis by contracting uterine spiral arterioles. Longer duration than natural PGF2α (methylation prevents inactivation by 15-hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase). Also causes smooth muscle contraction in GI tract and bronchi (side effects)
dosing: PPH: 250mcg IM (deep gluteal or thigh). Repeat every 15-90 minutes as needed (max 8 doses, total 2mg). Often effective after 1-3 doses. Alternative: dilute 250mcg in 10ml saline for intramyometrial injection (off-license). Medical termination of pregnancy (second trimester): IM dosing per protocol (not UK practice)
contraindications: Active cardiac/pulmonary/renal/hepatic disease. Acute pelvic inflammatory disease. Caution/relative contraindications: asthma (may cause severe bronchospasm - have bronchodilators ready, avoid if severe asthma), hypertension (may worsen), epilepsy (may lower seizure threshold), glaucoma, previous uterine surgery (rupture risk - but PPH indication often outweighs risk)
interactions: Other uterotonics (oxytocin, ergometrine, misoprostol) - additive effect (often used in combination for PPH, but caution). No significant CYP interactions
monitoring: Uterine tone (palpate fundus), vaginal bleeding (volume, cessation). Vital signs: BP (may ↑ or ↓), HR, SpO2. Respiratory status (bronchospasm risk, especially in asthma - auscultate, watch for wheeze/desaturation). Temperature (fever common). Fluid balance (haemorrhage). FBC, coagulation (if severe PPH). Consider arterial blood gas if respiratory concerns
pregnancy: Used specifically in postpartum setting for PPH. Not used in pregnancy (abortifacient). Contraindicated antepartum (not for induction of labour in UK - uterine rupture risk)
sideEffects: Very common: nausea/vomiting (>50%), diarrhoea (GI smooth muscle stimulation), fever/chills (10-40%, transient - prostaglandin-mediated hypothalamic effect), flushing. Common: hypertension (transient), tachycardia, headache, dizziness. Important serious: bronchospasm (especially pre-existing asthma - can be severe/fatal, have salbutamol/adrenaline ready), pulmonary oedema (rare, fluid overload + capillary leak), uterine rupture (if excessive dosing/obstructed labour - not typical PPH scenario). Rare: anaphylaxis
pharmacokinetics: Deep IM injection. Rapid absorption, peak 15-30 min. Metabolized in lungs, liver, kidneys. Half-life: <1h. Duration of action: 2-4h (longer than natural PGF2α due to 15-methyl substitution preventing enzymatic degradation)
clinicalPearls: Brand: Hemabate. Second-line uterotonic for PPH (after oxytocin, before/with ergometrine, alongside misoprostol). PPH management: first-line oxytocin (IV/IM) → if unsuccessful, add ergometrine (if no hypertension) and/or carboprost and/or misoprostol → if persistent, surgical (balloon tamponade, uterine artery embolization, B-Lynch suture, hysterectomy). Carboprost often very effective when oxytocin/ergometrine fail. IM administration convenient (no IV access needed). ASTHMA: relative contraindication - severe bronchospasm risk. If severe asthma, avoid (use misoprostol, ergometrine, or surgical). If mild-moderate asthma and PPH life-threatening, may use with extreme caution, have bronchodilators/adrenaline ready, ITU support. Salbutamol nebulizers on standby. SIDE EFFECTS: nausea/vomiting, diarrhoea common but not dangerous (reassure, antiemetics). Fever common (10-40%) - transient, prostaglandin-mediated, not infection. DOSING: 250mcg IM every 15-90 min (tailored to response). Max 8 doses (2mg total). Often effective after 1-3 doses. If >3 doses, consider alternative measures (surgical). INTRAMYOMETRIAL injection: some use diluted carboprost directly into myometrium (off-license) - may be more effective, faster onset. Combination therapy: often used with misoprostol (different mechanisms - additive effect). Oxytocin continues throughout. Ergometrine if no hypertension. Can cause significant hypertension (monitor BP) - avoid ergometrine if carboprost causes BP rise. Part of PPH algorithm (WHO, RCOG): massage → oxytocin → add ergometrine/carboprost/misoprostol → surgical. Ensure large-bore IV access, fluids, blood products if severe. Senior obstetrician, anaesthetist involvement
indication: Postpartum haemorrhage refractory to oxytocin (second-line uterotonic). Medical termination of pregnancy (second trimester - not standard UK practice)
